title: TÜRKİYE
GEOGRAPHY
BASICS
hook: Think you know where Turkey sits on the map? Five quick questions. The last one fools almost everyone!

qs.q: Türkiye lies on which two continents?
qs.say: Turkey lies on which two continents?
qs.fact: Most of Türkiye is in Asia; a small part, Thrace, is in Europe.
qs.sayAnswer: Europe and Asia! Most of Turkey is in Asia, and a small part, called Thrace, is in Europe.

qs.q: Which strait splits Istanbul between Europe and Asia?
qs.say: Which strait splits Istanbul between Europe and Asia?
qs.fact: The Bosphorus links the Black Sea to the Sea of Marmara.
qs.sayAnswer: The Bosphorus! It links the Black Sea to the Sea of Marmara.

qs.q: How many geographical regions is Türkiye divided into?
qs.say: How many geographical regions is Turkey divided into?
qs.fact: The seven regions were set by Türkiye's First Geography Congress.
qs.sayAnswer: Seven! The 7 regions were set by Turkey's First Geography Congress.

qs.q: How many countries share a land border with Türkiye?
qs.say: How many countries share a land border with Turkey?
qs.fact: Greece, Bulgaria, Georgia, Armenia, Azerbaijan, Iran, Iraq and Syria.
qs.sayAnswer: Eight! Greece, Bulgaria, Georgia, Armenia, Azerbaijan, Iran, Iraq and Syria.

qs.q: Which sea lies entirely inside Türkiye?
qs.say: Which sea lies entirely inside Turkey?
qs.fact: The Sea of Marmara connects the Black Sea and the Aegean.
qs.sayAnswer: The Sea of Marmara! It connects the Black Sea and the Aegean, and it is all Turkish.

title: HOW WELL
DO YOU KNOW
ISTANBUL?
hook: Istanbul, the city on two continents. Five questions, three seconds each. Can you get the last one?

qs.q: By what name was Istanbul long known in the West?
qs.say: By what name was Istanbul long known in the West?
qs.fact: Before that it was Byzantium. Istanbul became the official name in 1930.
qs.sayAnswer: Constantinople! Before that it was Byzantium. Istanbul became the official name in 1930.

qs.q: Which emperor built Hagia Sophia, completed in 537?
qs.say: Which emperor built Hagia Sophia, completed in the year 537?
qs.fact: It was built in less than six years, starting in 532.
qs.sayAnswer: Justinian the First! It was built in less than 6 years, starting in 532.

qs.q: Which Istanbul tower was built by the Genoese in 1348?
qs.say: Which Istanbul tower was built by the Genoese in 1348?
qs.fact: Galata Tower was first called the Tower of Christ.
qs.sayAnswer: Galata Tower! It was first called the Tower of Christ.

qs.q: About how many shops fill Istanbul's Grand Bazaar?
qs.say: About how many shops fill Istanbul's Grand Bazaar?
qs.fact: The Grand Bazaar has 61 covered streets and over 4,000 shops.
qs.sayAnswer: Four thousand! The Grand Bazaar has 61 covered streets and more than 4000 shops.

qs.q: Istanbul's Tünel is the world's second-oldest subway. When did it open?
qs.say: Istanbul's Tunel is the world's second-oldest subway. When did it open?
qs.fact: It opened in 1875. Only London's Underground is older.
qs.sayAnswer: 1875! Only London's Underground is older.

title: TURKISH
CITIES
QUIZ
hook: Five Turkish cities, five questions. Easy at the start, but the last one catches most people out!

qs.q: In which city is Anıtkabir, the mausoleum of Atatürk?
qs.say: In which city is Anit-kabir, the mausoleum of Ataturk?
qs.fact: Anıtkabir was completed in 1953 in the capital, Ankara.
qs.sayAnswer: Ankara! The mausoleum was completed in 1953 in the capital.

qs.q: Which Turkish city was known in antiquity as Smyrna?
qs.say: Which Turkish city was known in ancient times as Smyrna?
qs.fact: İzmir is Türkiye's third most populous city, on the Aegean coast.
qs.sayAnswer: Izmeer! It is Turkey's third most populous city, on the Aegean coast.

qs.q: Which city holds Rumi's tomb and is home of the whirling dervishes?
qs.say: Which city holds Rumi's tomb and is home of the whirling dervishes?
qs.fact: Rumi's turquoise-domed tomb is now the Mevlana Museum.
qs.sayAnswer: Konya! Rumi's turquoise-domed tomb is now the Mevlana Museum.

qs.q: Licence plates starting with 01 belong to which province?
qs.say: Licence plates starting with zero one belong to which province?
qs.fact: Adana is 01, Ankara is 06 and Istanbul is 34.
qs.sayAnswer: Adana! Adana is zero one, Ankara is zero six, and Istanbul is 34.

qs.q: Which is Türkiye's smallest province by area?
qs.say: Which is Turkey's smallest province by area?
qs.fact: Yalova covers only about 850 square kilometres.
qs.sayAnswer: Yalova! It covers only about 850 square kilometres.

title: MOUNTAINS
& VOLCANOES
OF TÜRKİYE
hook: Turkey is a land of mountains and sleeping volcanoes. Five questions. Watch out for the tricky last one!

qs.q: Which mountain range runs parallel to Türkiye's Mediterranean coast?
qs.say: Which mountain range runs parallel to Turkey's Mediterranean coast?
qs.fact: The Taurus separate the Mediterranean coast from the central plateau.
qs.sayAnswer: The Taurus Mountains! They separate the Mediterranean coast from the central plateau.

qs.q: Uludağ, a famous ski mountain, rises above which city?
qs.say: Oo-loo-dah, a famous ski mountain, rises above which city?
qs.fact: At 2,543 m, Uludağ is the highest mountain of the Marmara region.
qs.sayAnswer: Bursa! At 2543 meters, it is the highest mountain of the Marmara region.

qs.q: Which snow-capped volcano towers over the city of Kayseri?
qs.say: Which snow-capped volcano towers over the city of Kai-seri?
qs.fact: Erciyes, about 3,917 m, is the highest peak of Central Anatolia.
qs.sayAnswer: Mount Air-jee-yes! At about 3917 meters, it is the highest peak of Central Anatolia.

qs.q: What crowns the summit of Mount Nemrut in Adıyaman?
qs.say: What crowns the summit of Mount Nemroot in Adi-yaman?
qs.fact: King Antiochus I of Commagene built it in the 1st century BC.
qs.sayAnswer: Giant stone heads! King Antiochus the First of Commagene built it in the first century B C.

qs.q: A second Mount Nemrut, a volcano with a crater lake, is in which province?
qs.say: A second Mount Nemroot, a volcano with a crater lake, is in which province?
qs.fact: This Nemrut's caldera, beside Lake Van, is the largest in Türkiye.
qs.sayAnswer: Bitlis! This Nemroot's caldera, beside Lake Van, is the largest in Turkey.

title: LAKES
& RIVERS
OF TÜRKİYE
hook: Rivers, lakes and one word you use without knowing it is Turkish geography. Five questions, go!

qs.q: Which two great rivers rise in Türkiye and flow on to Iraq?
qs.say: Which two great rivers rise in Turkey and flow on to Iraq?
qs.fact: They meet in Iraq and flow into the Persian Gulf.
qs.sayAnswer: The Euphrates and the Tigris! They meet in Iraq and flow into the Persian Gulf.

qs.q: Which giant salt lake lies in the heart of Central Anatolia?
qs.say: Which giant salt lake lies in the heart of Central Anatolia?
qs.fact: Tuz means salt. It is Türkiye's second-largest lake.
qs.sayAnswer: Lake Tooz! Tooz means salt, and it is Turkey's second-largest lake.

qs.q: Which is the longest river flowing entirely within Türkiye?
qs.say: Which is the longest river flowing entirely within Turkey?
qs.fact: Kızılırmak means Red River. It flows into the Black Sea.
qs.sayAnswer: The Kizil-irmak! Its name means Red River, and it flows into the Black Sea.

qs.q: Which Turkish river gave English the word "meander"?
qs.say: Which Turkish river gave English the word meander?
qs.fact: The ancient Greeks called this winding river the Maeander.
qs.sayAnswer: The Menderes! The ancient Greeks called this winding river the Meander.

qs.q: Which is Türkiye's largest freshwater lake?
qs.say: Which is Turkey's largest freshwater lake?
qs.fact: Lake Beyşehir covers about 650 km² in Konya and Isparta provinces.
qs.sayAnswer: Lake Bay-sheh-heer! It covers about 650 square kilometres in Konya and Isparta provinces.

title: SEAS
& COASTS
OF TÜRKİYE
hook: Turkey has sea on three sides. Do you really know its coasts? Five questions, starting easy!

qs.q: Which sea lies along Türkiye's northern coast?
qs.say: Which sea lies along Turkey's northern coast?
qs.fact: The eastern Black Sea coast is the rainiest part of Türkiye.
qs.sayAnswer: The Black Sea! Its eastern coast is the rainiest part of Turkey.

qs.q: Which strait links the Aegean Sea to the Sea of Marmara?
qs.say: Which strait links the Aegean Sea to the Sea of Marmara?
qs.fact: In antiquity the Dardanelles were known as the Hellespont.
qs.sayAnswer: The Dardanelles! In ancient times they were known as the Hellespont.

qs.q: Which city is the tourism capital of the Turkish Riviera?
qs.say: Which city is the tourism capital of the Turkish Riviera?
qs.fact: Antalya is Türkiye's biggest international sea resort.
qs.sayAnswer: Antalya! It is Turkey's biggest international sea resort.

qs.q: The famous Blue Lagoon of Ölüdeniz is near which town?
qs.say: The famous Blue Lagoon of Uh-lu-deniz is near which town?
qs.fact: Ölüdeniz means Dead Sea, named for its calm waters.
qs.sayAnswer: Fet-hee-yeh! The lagoon's Turkish name means Dead Sea, because its waters are so calm.

qs.q: Who built Bodrum's seaside castle in the 15th century?
qs.say: Who built Bodrum's seaside castle in the 15th century?
qs.fact: The knights reused stones from the ancient Mausoleum of Halicarnassus.
qs.sayAnswer: The Knights of Saint John! They reused stones from the ancient Mausoleum of Halicarnassus.

title: TÜRKİYE'S
NEIGHBOURS
QUIZ
hook: Eight neighbours, five questions. Almost nobody knows which border is the shortest. Do you?

qs.q: Which of these countries does NOT border Türkiye?
qs.say: Which of these countries does not border Turkey?
qs.fact: Türkiye has eight land neighbours. Romania is across the Black Sea.
qs.sayAnswer: Romania! Turkey has 8 land neighbours, and Romania lies across the Black Sea.

qs.q: Which eastern neighbour of Türkiye is this?
qs.say: Which eastern neighbour of Turkey is this?
qs.fact: Iran borders Türkiye in the east, not far from Mount Ararat.
qs.sayAnswer: Iran! It borders Turkey in the east, not far from Mount Ararat.

qs.q: With which country does Türkiye share its longest land border?
qs.say: With which country does Turkey share its longest land border?
qs.fact: The border with Syria stretches for more than 800 kilometres.
qs.sayAnswer: Syria! That border stretches for more than 800 kilometres.

qs.q: The Meriç (Maritsa) river forms much of Türkiye's border with whom?
qs.say: The Maritsa river forms much of Turkey's border with which country?
qs.fact: The river is called Meriç in Turkish and Evros in Greek.
qs.sayAnswer: Greece! The river is called Meh-rich in Turkish, and Evros in Greek.

qs.q: With which country does Türkiye share its shortest land border?
qs.say: With which country does Turkey share its shortest land border?
qs.fact: The border with Azerbaijan's Nakhchivan is less than 20 km long.
qs.sayAnswer: Azerbaijan! The border with its Nakhchivan region is less than 20 kilometres long.

title: UNESCO
TREASURES
OF TÜRKİYE
hook: Turkey is packed with UNESCO World Heritage sites. Five questions. The last one stumps even history fans!

qs.q: What does the name Pamukkale mean?
qs.say: What does the name Pamook-kaleh mean?
qs.fact: Its white terraces are travertine left by hot spring water.
qs.sayAnswer: Cotton Castle! Its white terraces are made of travertine, left by hot spring water.

qs.q: The Library of Celsus stands in which ancient city?
qs.say: The Library of Celsus stands in which ancient city?
qs.fact: Ephesus, in İzmir Province, joined the UNESCO list in 2015.
qs.sayAnswer: Ephesus! It is in Izmeer Province, and it joined the UNESCO list in 2015.

qs.q: Which UNESCO-listed town is famous for its Ottoman-era houses?
qs.say: Which UNESCO-listed town is famous for its Ottoman-era houses?
qs.fact: Safranbolu is named after saffron, once grown and traded there.
qs.sayAnswer: Saf-ran-bolu! It is named after saffron, which was once grown and traded there.

qs.q: Which 9,000-year-old Neolithic town was found near Konya?
qs.say: Which 9000 year old Stone Age town was found near Konya?
qs.fact: Most of its houses were entered through a hole in the roof.
qs.sayAnswer: Chatal-hoy-uk! Most of its houses were entered through a hole in the roof.

qs.q: The UNESCO-listed Great Mosque and Hospital of Divriği is in which province?
qs.say: The UNESCO-listed Great Mosque and Hospital of Div-ree is in which province?
qs.fact: Built in 1228-29, it was among Türkiye's first UNESCO sites in 1985.
qs.sayAnswer: See-vas! Built around 1228, it was among Turkey's first UNESCO sites in 1985.

title: ANCIENT
ANATOLIA
QUIZ
hook: Troy, the Hittites and the world's oldest monuments are all in Turkey. Five questions on ancient Anatolia!

qs.q: The ruins of which legendary city lie in Çanakkale Province?
qs.say: The ruins of which legendary city lie in Cha-nak-ka-leh Province?
qs.fact: Heinrich Schliemann began excavating Troy in 1870.
qs.sayAnswer: Troy! Heinrich Schliemann began excavating it in 1870.

qs.q: Göbekli Tepe, with the world's oldest known megaliths, is near which city?
qs.say: Go-beck-lee Teh-peh, with the world's oldest known megaliths, is near which city?
qs.fact: Its great stone pillars were raised more than 11,000 years ago.
qs.sayAnswer: Shan-luh-oor-fa! Its great stone pillars were raised more than 11000 years ago.

qs.q: Hattusa was the capital of which Bronze Age empire?
qs.say: Hat-too-sha was the capital of which Bronze Age empire?
qs.fact: Hattusa's ruins lie near Boğazkale in Çorum Province.
qs.sayAnswer: The Hittite Empire! The ruins lie near Bo-az-kaleh, in Chorum Province.

qs.q: The Mausoleum at Halicarnassus stood in which modern Turkish town?
qs.say: The Mausoleum at Halicarnassus stood in which modern Turkish town?
qs.fact: It was the tomb of Mausolus, whose name gave us the word mausoleum.
qs.sayAnswer: Bodrum! It was the tomb of Mausolus, whose name gave us the word mausoleum.

qs.q: Which Anatolian kingdom is credited with minting the first coins?
qs.say: Which Anatolian kingdom is credited with minting the first coins?
qs.fact: Lydia's capital was Sardis; its early coins were made of electrum.
qs.sayAnswer: Lydia! Its capital was Sardis, and its early coins were made of electrum, a mix of gold and silver.

title: OTTOMAN
EMPIRE
QUIZ
hook: Six centuries of Ottoman history in five questions. Most people get the last one wrong!

qs.q: Which sultan conquered Constantinople in 1453?
qs.say: Which sultan conquered Constantinople in 1453?
qs.fact: Mehmed the Conqueror was only 21 years old.
qs.sayAnswer: Mehmed the Second! Known as the Conqueror, he was only 21 years old.

qs.q: Which palace was home to Ottoman sultans for nearly four centuries?
qs.say: Which palace was home to Ottoman sultans for nearly four centuries?
qs.fact: Topkapı Palace became a museum in 1924.
qs.sayAnswer: Top-kapuh Palace! It became a museum in 1924.

qs.q: Who was the great architect of Istanbul's Süleymaniye Mosque?
qs.say: Who was the great architect of Istanbul's Sue-lay-mah-nee-yeh Mosque?
qs.fact: Sinan also built the Selimiye Mosque in Edirne, a UNESCO site.
qs.sayAnswer: Mee-mar See-nan! He also built the Selimiye Mosque in Eh-deer-neh, a UNESCO site.

qs.q: Which Ottoman sultan reigned the longest?
qs.say: Which Ottoman sultan reigned the longest?
qs.fact: Suleiman the Magnificent ruled for 46 years, from 1520 to 1566.
qs.sayAnswer: Suleiman the Magnificent! He ruled for 46 years, from 1520 to 1566.

qs.q: Which city was the Ottoman capital just before Istanbul?
qs.say: Which city was the Ottoman capital just before Istanbul?
qs.fact: Many guess Bursa, but Edirne was the capital until the 1450s.
qs.sayAnswer: Eh-deer-neh! Many people guess Bursa, but Eh-deer-neh was the capital until the 1450s.

title: ATATÜRK
& THE
REPUBLIC
hook: How much do you know about Ataturk and the birth of modern Turkey? Five questions on key dates!

qs.q: Who was the founder and first president of the Republic of Türkiye?
qs.say: Who was the founder and first president of the Republic of Turkey?
qs.fact: Atatürk served as president from 1923 until his death in 1938.
qs.sayAnswer: Mustafa Kemal Ataturk! He served as president from 1923 until his death in 1938.

qs.q: On which date was the Republic of Türkiye proclaimed?
qs.say: On which date was the Republic of Turkey proclaimed?
qs.fact: 29 October is celebrated every year as Republic Day.
qs.sayAnswer: The 29th of October, 1923! It is celebrated every year as Republic Day.

qs.q: In which city was Atatürk born in 1881?
qs.say: In which city was Ataturk born in 1881?
qs.fact: His birthplace, then called Salonica, is now in Greece.
qs.sayAnswer: Thessaloniki! His birthplace, then called Salonica, is now in Greece.

qs.q: In which year did Türkiye adopt its Latin-based alphabet?
qs.say: In which year did Turkey adopt its Latin-based alphabet?
qs.fact: The Turkish alphabet has 29 letters, with no Q, W or X.
qs.sayAnswer: 1928! The Turkish alphabet has 29 letters, with no Q, W or X.

qs.q: In which year did Mustafa Kemal receive the surname Atatürk?
qs.say: In which year did Mustafa Kemal receive the surname Ataturk?
qs.fact: Parliament gave him the name, meaning Father of the Turks.
qs.sayAnswer: 1934! Parliament gave him the name, which means Father of the Turks.

title: TURKISH
FOOD & DRINK
QUIZ
hook: Hungry? Five tasty questions about Turkish food and drink. The last ingredient will surprise you!

qs.q: Which salty Turkish drink is made from yogurt and water?
qs.say: Which salty Turkish drink is made from yogurt and water?
qs.fact: Ayran is simply yogurt, water and a pinch of salt.
qs.sayAnswer: Eye-ran! It is simply yogurt, water and a pinch of salt.

qs.q: Which city is Türkiye's baklava capital?
qs.say: Which city is Turkey's baklava capital?
qs.fact: Antep baklava won protected status from the EU in 2013.
qs.sayAnswer: Gazi-antep! Its pistachio baklava won protected status from the European Union in 2013.

qs.q: Türkiye is the world's top producer of which nut?
qs.say: Turkey is the world's top producer of which nut?
qs.fact: In 2023 Türkiye grew more than half of the world's hazelnuts.
qs.sayAnswer: Hazelnuts! In 2023, Turkey grew more than half of the world's hazelnuts.

qs.q: "Kahvaltı", the Turkish word for breakfast, literally means what?
qs.say: Kah-val-tuh, the Turkish word for breakfast, literally means what?
qs.fact: Yet the star drink of a Turkish breakfast is black tea.
qs.sayAnswer: Before coffee! And yet the star drink of a Turkish breakfast is black tea.

qs.q: Stretchy Maraş ice cream is thickened with salep. What is salep made from?
qs.say: Stretchy Marash ice cream is thickened with salep. What is salep made from?
qs.fact: Salep is a flour ground from the tubers of wild orchids.
qs.sayAnswer: Orchid tubers! Salep is a flour ground from the tubers of wild orchids.

title: NATURE
& WILDLIFE
OF TÜRKİYE
hook: Swimming cats, giant dogs and one of the world's rarest birds. Five questions on Turkey's wildlife!

qs.q: Which big guardian dog comes from Sivas Province?
qs.say: Which big guardian dog comes from See-vas Province?
qs.fact: Kangals have guarded flocks from wolves for centuries.
qs.sayAnswer: The Kangal! Kangals have guarded flocks from wolves for centuries.

qs.q: Which flower reached Europe from the Ottoman Empire in the 1500s?
qs.say: Which flower reached Europe from the Ottoman Empire in the 1500s?
qs.fact: The word tulip is thought to come from a word for turban.
qs.sayAnswer: The tulip! The word tulip is thought to come from a word for turban.

qs.q: Which Turkish cat is nicknamed the "swimming cat"?
qs.say: Which Turkish cat is nicknamed the swimming cat?
qs.fact: Van cats, from the Lake Van region, can have odd-coloured eyes.
qs.sayAnswer: The Van cat! Van cats, from the Lake Van region, can have odd-coloured eyes.

qs.q: İztuzu Beach near Dalyan is a protected nesting site for which animal?
qs.say: Iz-too-zoo Beach, near Dalyan, is a protected nesting site for which animal?
qs.fact: The beach has been protected since 1988.
qs.sayAnswer: Loggerhead turtles! The beach has been protected since 1988.

qs.q: Which very rare bird is protected at Birecik in Şanlıurfa?
qs.say: Which very rare bird is protected at Bee-reh-jik, in Shan-luh-oor-fa?
qs.fact: A breeding station has cared for Birecik's bald ibises since the 1970s.
qs.sayAnswer: The northern bald ibis! A breeding station has cared for the birds there since the 1970s.

title: TÜRKİYE'S
BIGGEST
RECORDS
hook: The biggest, the longest, the deepest. Five record breakers from Turkey. Can you score five out of five?

qs.q: Which is Türkiye's most populous city?
qs.say: Which is Turkey's most populous city?
qs.fact: More than 15 million people live in Istanbul.
qs.sayAnswer: Istanbul! More than 15 million people live there.

qs.q: What world record does the 1915 Çanakkale Bridge hold?
qs.say: What world record does the 1915 Cha-nak-ka-leh Bridge hold?
qs.fact: Its main span is 2,023 m, the longest of any suspension bridge.
qs.sayAnswer: The longest main span! At 2023 meters, it is the longest of any suspension bridge.

qs.q: Which is Türkiye's largest island?
qs.say: Which is Turkey's largest island?
qs.fact: Gökçeada, in the Aegean Sea, is also known as Imbros.
qs.sayAnswer: Gok-cheh-ada! This island in the Aegean Sea is also known as Imbros.

qs.q: Marmaray, the rail tunnel under the Bosphorus, holds which record?
qs.say: Marmaray, the rail tunnel under the Bosphorus, holds which record?
qs.fact: It lies up to 60 m below sea level and opened in 2013.
qs.sayAnswer: The deepest immersed tube tunnel! It lies up to 60 meters below sea level, and opened in 2013.

qs.q: Which Turkish province has the longest coastline?
qs.say: Which Turkish province has the longest coastline?
qs.fact: Muğla's twisting coast of bays and peninsulas runs over 1,000 km.
qs.sayAnswer: Moo-la! Its twisting coast of bays and peninsulas runs for more than 1000 kilometres.

title: HOW WELL
DO YOU KNOW
CAPPADOCIA?
hook: Balloons, fairy chimneys and cities hidden underground. Five questions on Cappadocia. Ready?

qs.q: What fills the sky over Cappadocia at sunrise?
qs.say: What fills the sky over Cappadocia at sunrise?
qs.fact: Balloons drift over the valleys around Göreme at dawn.
qs.sayAnswer: Hot-air balloons! They drift over the valleys around Guh-reh-meh at dawn.

qs.q: What are Cappadocia's tall rock spires called?
qs.say: What are Cappadocia's tall rock spires called?
qs.fact: Wind and water carved them from soft volcanic rock.
qs.sayAnswer: Fairy chimneys! Wind and water carved them from soft volcanic rock.

qs.q: Göreme, the heart of Cappadocia, is in which province?
qs.say: Guh-reh-meh, the heart of Cappadocia, is in which province?
qs.fact: Göreme National Park has been a UNESCO site since 1985.
qs.sayAnswer: Nev-sheh-heer! Guh-reh-meh National Park has been a UNESCO site since 1985.

qs.q: Cappadocia's soft rock was laid down by what?
qs.say: Cappadocia's soft rock was laid down by what?
qs.fact: Erciyes, Hasan and Göllüdağ volcanoes blanketed the region.
qs.sayAnswer: Volcanic eruptions! Three ancient volcanoes, including Mount Air-jee-yes, blanketed the region.

qs.q: About how many people could Derinkuyu underground city shelter?
qs.say: About how many people could Deh-rin-koo-yoo underground city shelter?
qs.fact: Derinkuyu goes down about 85 metres below the surface.
qs.sayAnswer: Twenty thousand! The city goes down about 85 meters below the surface.

title: AEGEAN &
MEDITERRANEAN
COAST QUIZ
hook: Turquoise water, ancient ruins and a mountain that is on fire. Five questions on Turkey's sunny coasts!

qs.q: Which sea washes Türkiye's west coast?
qs.say: Which sea washes Turkey's west coast?
qs.fact: Ancient Ephesus and Troy both lie near the Aegean coast.
qs.sayAnswer: The Aegean Sea! Ancient Ephesus and Troy both lie near the Aegean coast.

qs.q: What is a "gulet", the star of the Blue Cruise?
qs.say: What is a goolet, the star of the Blue Cruise?
qs.fact: Gulets are built mainly in Bodrum and Marmaris.
qs.sayAnswer: A wooden sailing boat! Goolets are built mainly in Bodrum and Marmaris.

qs.q: The Lycian Way hiking trail runs between Fethiye and which city?
qs.say: The Lycian Way hiking trail runs between Fet-hee-yeh and which city?
qs.fact: The waymarked trail along the ancient Lycian coast opened in 1999.
qs.sayAnswer: Antalya! The waymarked trail along the ancient Lycian coast opened in 1999.

qs.q: St Nicholas, the original Santa Claus, was bishop of which city?
qs.say: Saint Nicholas, the original Santa Claus, was bishop of which city?
qs.fact: Myra is today's Demre in Antalya. He was born in nearby Patara.
qs.sayAnswer: Myra! That is today's Demre, in Antalya, and he was born in nearby Patara.

qs.q: What makes Yanartaş, near Olympos, so unusual?
qs.say: What makes Yanar-tash, near Olympos, so unusual?
qs.fact: Natural gas fires have burned there for at least 2,500 years.
qs.sayAnswer: Flames from the rock! Natural gas fires have burned there for at least 2500 years.

title: BLACK SEA
REGION
QUIZ
hook: Green mountains, tea gardens and a famous philosopher. Five questions on Turkey's Black Sea coast!

qs.q: Which crop covers the hills of Rize on the Black Sea?
qs.say: Which crop covers the hills of Ree-zeh, on the Black Sea?
qs.fact: Most Turkish tea comes from Rize Province.
qs.sayAnswer: Tea! Most Turkish tea comes from Ree-zeh Province.

qs.q: Which small fish is the star of Black Sea cooking?
qs.say: Which small fish is the star of Black Sea cooking?
qs.fact: Trabzon is famous across Türkiye for its hamsi.
qs.sayAnswer: Hamsi, the anchovy! The city of Trabzon is famous across Turkey for it.

qs.q: Which monastery clings to a cliff near Trabzon?
qs.say: Which monastery clings to a cliff near Trabzon?
qs.fact: Sümela sits about 1,200 m up in the Pontic Mountains.
qs.sayAnswer: Soo-meh-la! It sits about 1200 meters up in the Pontic Mountains.

qs.q: Which bowed string instrument is typical of the Black Sea coast?
qs.say: Which bowed string instrument is typical of the Black Sea coast?
qs.fact: The Black Sea kemençe has three strings and is played upright.
qs.sayAnswer: The keh-men-cheh! It has 3 strings and is played upright.

qs.q: Which Black Sea city was the birthplace of the philosopher Diogenes?
